assessment:
Three wishes. Three cards in the 99 search the library for something other than a land, enumerated by oracle text: Vampiric Tutor ({B}, instant, any card, on top, you lose 2), Demonic Tutor ({1}{B}, sorcery, any card, to hand) and Diabolic Intent ({1}{B}, sorcery, any card, to hand, sacrifice a creature as an additional cost). The five fetch lands search for lands, and Path to Exile hands its search to the creature's controller.

What they are for now. v3.0.0 has no two-card line to fetch (deck-facts: 0 contained combo lines). The game ends by accumulation: bodies, a free outlet, death drains that also gain, and a converter (Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose; Sanguine Bond; Enduring Tenacity; Marauding Blight-Priest) that bills the gain. The tutors fill whichever piece the board lacks, or find the one verified finisher, Bloodletter of Aclazotz under Sanctum Seeker (stack 003: 14 a seat from seven attackers).

Where not to point them. Drawn in more than 60% of games unassisted (goldfish, seed 42, 10,000 games, decklist 1df3a335): a castable Vampire 86.4%, ramp 77.2%, a draw engine 75.9%, a free outlet 71.6%, a death drain 62.9%, protection 62.5%, a converter 61.8%. Below that: a token multiplier 36.5%, the noncreature answer 21.5% (Anguished Unmaking alone; 59.9% assisted, the widest assisted gap here), Bloodletter with Sanctum Seeker 4.4% (26.7% assisted). The assisted column credits all three tutors together, so no figure here is one tutor's own.

Which converter. Many small gains (Cruel Celebrant, Blood Artist, Wispdrinker Vampire, extort): Marauding Blight-Priest, 1 from every seat per gain. One large gain (Vish Kal's or Kalitas's lifelink, Vito's own lifelink activation, Anje's 2): Vito, Sanguine Bond or Tenacity, which aim that much at one seat. Creature removal shown: Bond, never a creature. Enchantment removal shown: Vito or Blight-Priest.

Timing. Vampiric puts the card on top: cast it at the end step of the player to your right, and only when you can cast the card the turn it arrives. Demonic and Intent put it in hand in your main phase; Demonic plus a three-mana converter is five, plus Bloodletter six. Mean available mana reads 5.15 on turn five, 5.853 on six, 6.54 on seven. Intent is also a death: its cost fires every death drain before the search resolves.

The life. Vampiric costs 2, Unmaking 3, Midnight Reaper 1 a card, the painlands every turn. Stop paying the turn a pinger or a drain seat has you in range.

tutors.notes: {B}, instant, any card, on top, 2 life; it reveals nothing. Cast it at the end step of the player to your right so the card is your next draw. Count the mana for the fetched card before you cast it. Master of Dark Rites pays {B}{B}{B} toward a Vampire, Cleric or Demon spell off a sacrificed creature: Bloodletter, Vito, Blight-Priest and Kalitas qualify; Sanguine Bond (an enchantment) and Enduring Tenacity (a Snake Glimmer) do not.

targets.scenario: End step of the player to your right, turn seven. Your board: Sanctum Seeker, Edgar Markov (cast on turn six), Master of Dark Rites and five eminence tokens, all untapping next turn. Opponents at 26, 19 and 14; none has shown an instant-speed creature answer this game. Six lands, one untapped now.
targets.why:
The closing fetch. Stack 003 is the deck's one verified kill: on your turn each Sanctum Seeker trigger costs each opponent 2, not 1, and your gain is not doubled. Next turn, precombat, Master of Dark Rites sacrifices a token for {B}{B}{B} and one land finishes Bloodletter's {1}{B}{B}{B}. Bloodletter has no haste and need not attack: the doubling reads whose turn it is. Attack with Seeker, Edgar and the four remaining tokens: six triggers, 12 a seat before blockers. 14 goes to 2, 19 to 7, 26 to 14, and combat follows with Edgar's counter on every attacker. The stack proves the per-trigger arithmetic, not this board's outcome.

Rates: Bloodletter with Seeker is drawn in 4.4% of games, 1.6% by turn six, mean turn 6.906; 26.7% with a tutor. Bloodletter is the route's single point of failure, so if a seat has shown instant-speed removal, fetch it the turn Edgar is on the battlefield and Flawless Maneuver is free.

citations.quote: Effects that use the word “instead” are replacement effects.
An ability triggers only once each time its trigger event occurs. However, it can trigger repeatedly if one event contains multiple occurrences.

targets.scenario: End step of the player to your right, turn five. Your board: Edgar Markov, Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose, Cruel Celebrant, Sanctum Seeker and four tokens; no free outlet. The seat to your left plays white control, has swept once this game, and passed this turn with five open. Five lands, one untapped now.
targets.why:
The behind fetch. With no outlet the wipe is not your drain, it is your board. Flawless Maneuver and Akroma's Will make creatures indestructible but do not beat an exile or -X/-X sweeper; Teferi's Protection is the one of the four held protection spells that does, and it phases out Vito with the rest. Draw it and hold {2}{W} through the left seat's turn. Stated assumption: five open after an earlier sweep is another sweep. If they cast nothing, you spent a tutor on insurance, which is the trade.

Protection is drawn in 62.5% of games, 45.3% by turn six, so it is not a thin component: fetch it only when the threat is named.

citations.quote: assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing

targets.scenario: End step of the player to your right, turn six. The seat to your left resolved an enchantment god that pings each opponent whenever a creature enters under its control (the log 005 shape); its devotion is too low for it to be a creature. You are at 17 with Cruel Celebrant, Vraan and three tokens. Five lands, one untapped now.
targets.why: The answer fetch. Anguished Unmaking is the deck's one exile for a noncreature permanent: drawn in 21.5% of games, 13.7% by turn six, 59.9% with a tutor, the widest assisted gap in the artifact. It is an instant: draw it and cast it on your turn for {1}{W}{B}, or hold it for their next entry burst. 2 life for the tutor and 3 for the Unmaking puts you at 12; that is acceptable only because the pinger leaves. Olivia's Wrath would shrink their tokens and leave the enchantment.

targets.scenario: End step of the player to your right, turn eight. Twilight Prophet has been on your battlefield since turn five and you control eleven permanents, so you have the city's blessing. Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose is out. Opponents at 18, 15 and 11. Seven lands, one untapped now.
targets.why:
The fetch nobody sees. In your upkeep Prophet reveals the top card, puts it in your hand, and each opponent loses its mana value while you gain that much. Vish Kal is mana value 7, the highest in the 99: 7 off every seat, and Vito aims your 7 gained at the seat at 11, which is now at 4, so it dies in your upkeep. Then Vish Kal is in hand, and you still take your draw step.

This is an oracle-text reading. The goldfish lists Twilight Prophet under drain_not_modelled and no stack walks the line. Whether Bloodletter doubles Prophet's loss in your upkeep is the same open question as the converters.

tutors.notes: {1}{B}, sorcery, any card, to hand. The card arrives in your main phase, so this is the same-turn tutor: count the fetched card's cost with it.

targets.scenario: Your turn five, precombat. Board: Cruel Celebrant, Viscera Seer, Wispdrinker Vampire and three eminence tokens; Edgar in the command zone. No converter in hand or play. Five lands and Arcane Signet: six mana. Opponents at 34, 31 and 29; nobody has shown enchantment removal.
targets.why:
The default fetch: the board has outlet and drain and lacks a converter. It makes many small gains, so Blight-Priest, 1 from every seat per gain, beats Vito's 1 at one seat. Demonic (2) plus Blight-Priest (3) is five of your six. Blight-Priest is a Vampire, so eminence mints a token; the trigger resolves before the spell, so Wispdrinker's drain on that token is not converted. From then on every token you sacrifice to Seer costs each seat 2: Celebrant's 1, and Blight-Priest's 1 on Celebrant's gain. Every later eminence token is 2 a seat through Wispdrinker the same way. That per-gain count is an oracle reading; no stack has run it.

Rates: a converter is drawn in 61.8% of games unassisted, 81.0% with a tutor; 44.5% and 63.6% by turn six.

targets.scenario: Your turn six, precombat. The seat to your right has six non-Vampire creatures, two of them 4/4s. You have Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet, Edgar Markov and three tokens: five Vampires. You are at 19. Six lands and Talisman of Indulgence: seven mana.
targets.why:
The behind fetch. Demonic (2) plus the Wrath (5) is seven. Each non-Vampire gets -5/-5; your five Vampires are untouched. With Kalitas out each of their nontoken creatures is exiled instead of dying and you get a 2/2 Zombie. The Wrath's -X/-X affects the creatures it saw on resolution, so the Zombies that arrive after it live.

The cost: their creatures are exiled, not killed, so Blood Artist and Vein Ripper would not fire on them, and the Zombies are non-Vampires your own Anowon will ask for. Without Kalitas the Wrath is still one-sided, and their deaths fire every death drain you have out.

citations.quote: Effects that use the word “instead” are replacement effects.
the set of objects it affects is determined when that continuous effect begins. After that point, the set won’t change.

targets.scenario: Your turn eight, precombat. Sanctum Seeker, Edgar Markov, Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose and five tokens on board, all able to attack. Opponents at 16, 12 and 9. Eight lands.
targets.why:
The closing fetch. Demonic (2) plus Bloodletter (4) is six of eight. Attack with Seeker, Edgar and the five tokens: seven triggers, each 2 a seat under Bloodletter, 14 off each (stack 003's arithmetic). The 12 and the 9 die before blockers; the 16 goes to 2. Each trigger also gains you 1, and Vito aims each 1 at the seat you name: aim at the 16. Seven undoubled 1s finish it before blockers. The text says Bloodletter doubles those too; no stack has run a converter under it, so do not need it.

Assume every held answer appears the turn you present this; with two open on any seat, hold Flawless Maneuver too.

citations.quote: assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing
An ability triggers only once each time its trigger event occurs. However, it can trigger repeatedly if one event contains multiple occurrences.

tutors.notes: {1}{B} plus a creature. The sacrifice is a cost, so the death happens as you cast it: every death drain and death draw fires before the search resolves. To hand, sorcery speed.

targets.scenario: Your turn five, precombat. Board: Bloodghast, Grim Haruspex, Cruel Celebrant and two tokens; no free outlet. A land in hand, not yet played. Five lands.
targets.why:
The default fetch, and the sacrifice nobody plans. Sacrifice Bloodghast as Intent's cost: Celebrant drains 1 from each seat and gains 1, and Haruspex draws because Bloodghast is a nontoken creature. Fetch Viscera Seer, play the land, and Bloodghast returns. Cast Seer for {B}: it is a Vampire, so eminence mints a token. Three mana bought a card, a drain, the outlet, a token, and Bloodghast is back to do it again.

A free outlet is drawn in 71.6% of games, so this is not a thin component. The fetch earns its place because it is one mana and turns on everything already on the board.

citations.quote: To sacrifice a permanent, its controller moves it from the battlefield directly to its owner’s graveyard.
The term dies means “is put into a graveyard from the battlefield.”

targets.scenario: Your turn seven. A sweeper last turn left you with Yahenni (kept indestructible) and two tokens made since. Your hand is two lands. Eight mana.
targets.why:
The behind fetch. The empty hand is the logged failure (001, 002, 003, 006). Sacrifice a token as the cost. Liliana costs six: two plus six is all eight. She draws on every creature of yours that dies, tokens included, which Midnight Reaper and Grim Haruspex do not. +1 for a Zombie now. When the next sweeper comes, sacrifice to Yahenni in response, and each body is a card. Keep one outlet and one draw body back for the rebuild.

A draw engine is drawn in 75.9% of games; the fetch is right here because the board has no card flow at all, not because the component is thin.

citations.quote: Hold the second outlet and one draw body back for the rebuild

targets.scenario: Your turn nine. Vish Kal, Blood Arbiter is on your battlefield with four +1/+1 counters (9/9, flying, lifelink); Edgar Markov and three tokens beside it. No converter. Opponents at 22, 18 and 12; none has an untapped flyer. A seat has destroyed two of your creatures this game; nobody has removed an enchantment. Seven lands.
targets.why:
The closing fetch. Sacrifice a token as the cost; Intent (2) plus Bond (5) is seven. Sacrifice the two remaining tokens to Vish Kal: two more counters, 11/11. Attack with Vish Kal and Edgar; Edgar's trigger makes it 12/12. Twelve lifelink damage to the seat at 22 is 12 gained, and Bond aims 12 at the seat at 12. Bond, not Vito: the table has shown creature removal, and Bond is never a creature.

An oracle reading, no stack. Removal on Vish Kal in response to the sacrifices loses the counters; hold Flawless Maneuver, free with Edgar out.

citations.quote: A card doesn’t have a controller unless that card represents a permanent or spell

gaps: Stack 003 is the one presentable checker-passed stack on v3.0.0. Every converter line here (Blight-Priest per gain event, Vito under Bloodletter, Bond off Vish Kal's lifelink, Twilight Prophet's reveal drain) is an oracle-text reading, status needs a stack scenario; engine.json's first two open questions already route the converter-under-Bloodletter and lifelink-event-count cases to resolve-stack.
Kalitas with Olivia's Wrath rests on 614.1a and 611.2c and the cards' text; no stack walks it. engine.json's Kalitas plus Anowon question is the nearest open item.

The goldfish's assisted column credits all three tutors as one wildcard filling one missing group. It does not model the 2 life, the sacrifice, the lost draw or the choice between two missing groups, so no assisted figure is one tutor's own.

Twilight Prophet's upkeep drain and Sanctum Seeker's attack drain are both outside the goldfish (meta: drain_not_modelled, combat_effects_not_modelled), so the Vampiric reveal line and both Bloodletter closes are unmeasured beyond the draw rates quoted.
Nothing measures fetch-versus-hold or how often a converter resolves with protection up. Every timing call here is coaching on top of measured draw rates.
No graveyard or land answer is in the 99 to fetch; Kalitas's exile replacement on their nontoken creatures is the nearest thing to graveyard denial.
